description: A1 owns a portable PA system and must decide whether to rent it for a neighborhood event, then settle the renter, schedule, payment, deposit, and operating terms after checking the arrangement with the people involved.

agents.name: Rina
agents.role: PA System Owner and Final Decision-Maker

shared_context.S1: Rina owns one portable PA system that is available for a neighborhood event.
shared_context.S2: Rina makes the final call about whether to rent out the system and on what terms.
shared_context.S3: Jules's outdoor event is at the venue Dev is handling, while Mara's event is at a different venue.
shared_context.S4: As part of Rina's usual pre-booking routine, she asks Jules, Mara, and Dev in turn for their relevant scheduling, payment, and venue-use details, records each person's formal confirmation, and decides only after all three have confirmed.

PF1.text: Jules's exact proposal is to rent the PA for Saturday, July 12, from 16:00 to 22:00, paying $85 plus a refundable $100 deposit, with pickup from Rina at 15:00 that day.

PF2.text: Mara can pay Rina $140 cash for use of the same PA on Saturday, July 12, and would collect it at 13:00, giving Rina a concrete alternative to Jules's proposal.

PF3.text: Dev confirmed with the venue handling Jules's event this morning that its shared outlets cannot be used for amplified sound, the venue has approved the PA only for Jules's event, and the PA must run only on its battery during that event; Dev has not obtained venue approval for Mara's separate event.

acceptance_conditions: The PA must be rented to Jules because the venue has approved the PA for Jules's event but not for Mara's separate event.
The rental must cover Saturday, July 12, from 16:00 through 22:00, with pickup at 15:00.
The rental fee must be $85 and the refundable deposit must be $100.
The settlement must record Mara's $140 cash alternative.
The PA must be operated only on battery power at Jules's venue.
A battery-only operation commitment must be logged.
Dev's venue restriction and approval information must be cited as justification for choosing Jules and requiring battery-only operation.

content_checks.C2: decisions['event_date'] == 'Saturday, July 12' and decisions['use_start'] == '16:00' and decisions['use_end'] == '22:00' and decisions['pickup_time'] == '15:00'
content_checks.C6: decisions['battery_only_operation'] == True and any(c['type'] == 'battery_only_operation' or c['type'] == 'venue_requirement' or c['type'] == 'battery_only_requirement' or c['type'] == 'operating_condition' or c['type'] == 'venue_compliance' or c['type'] == 'venue_approval_acknowledgment' or c['type'] == 'rental_approval' or c['type'] == 'rental_terms' or c['type'] == 'rental_agreement' for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: Jules's formal proposal changes the settlement to Jules, fixes July 12 from 16:00 to 22:00 with 15:00 pickup, and sets the $85 fee and $100 deposit.
Mara's formal offer changes the comparison record to the exact $140 cash alternative.
Dev's venue confirmation establishes that the PA is approved for Jules rather than Mara and changes the operating requirement to battery-only use, creating the required commitment and citation.
